newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '96 labour productivity growth falls.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '96 labour productivity growth falls.

text.p: The productivity of the Malaysian labour force rose 4.7 percent in 1996 compared to a rise of 5.3 percent in 1995, said the central bank, Bank Negara in its 1996 annual report published on Friday.

"Data on overall labour productivity growth, as measured by the ratio of gross domestic product to total employment, showed that productivity had moderated to increase by 4.7 percent in 1996, compared with 5.3 percent in 1995," said Bank Negara.
A set of government guidelines linking wage increases to productivity had been adopted in 1996, said the central bank in its report.
"Average real wages in the manufacturing sector increased by 8.9 percent in 1996 compared with increases in real labour productivity of six percent," it said.
